key: And God said unto Moses: ‘I AM THAT I AM’; and He said: ‘Thus shalt thou say unto the children of Israel: I AM hath sent me unto you.’
s: At the bush Moses asks what to answer when Israel ask God’s name; Rashi, on Exodus 3:14, reads it as a promise to be with Israel in this trouble and in later bondage to other kingdoms, the second withheld from them at Moses’ plea.

evidence.words: אֶהְיֶה עִמָּם בְּצָרָה זוֹ אֲשֶׁר אֶהְיֶה עִמָּם בְּשִׁעְבּוּד שְׁאָר מַלְכֻיּוֹת. אָמַר לְפָנָיו, רִבּוֹנוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם, מָה אֲנִי מַזְכִּיר לָהֶם צָרָה אַחֶרֶת? דַּיָּם בְּצָרָה זוֹ, אָמַר לוֹ יָפֶה אָמַרְתָּ, כה תאמר וגו'
evidence.gloss: I will be with them in this trouble, as I will be with them in their subjection to the other kingdoms. He said before Him: Master of the world, why should I remind them of another trouble? This trouble is enough for them. He said to him: You have spoken well; thus shalt thou say, etc.

reason: verse.js ok (Exodus 3:14, at 52,14). Rashi on 3:14 in the packet reads the name as God being with Israel in this trouble and in the coming subjection to other kingdoms; Moses objects that this trouble suffices, God agrees and gives only the short message. The sentence carries this without addition; plain sense (Moses at the bush asking the name, 3:13) is faithful and does not echo the verse. Rashbam, Sforno and Exodus Rabbah 3:6 read differently but the entry names only Rashi, correctly. entry-check ok.
